To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrogen ions in microaqueou phase during lipase-catalysed esterifications in non-aqueou media can be calculated by mass transfer equations and expressed as hydrogen numbers.

the number of hydrogen ions in the microaqueos phase is maintained to a minimum by the partitioning of the water of the microaques phase to the organic solvent and the dissociation of the water soluble acid in it.
the number of H+ ions present at the microaqueou phase was maintained to a safe minimum to avoid the inactivation of enzyme and that this number was controlled by various thermodynamic processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the thermodynamic factors operating on the enzyme in non-aqueoussolvents, the water of reaction being present in the micro aqueous phase, the partition of acid between the organic and micro aqueous phase and the dissociation of the same in the micro aqueoussolvent.

the study of the role of hydrogen ion in the microaqueou phase in non-aqueou systems and the thermodynamic factors which operate in the system to maintain the hydrogen ion concentration in the microaqueos phase to a safe minimum.
the study of the microaqueos phase in non-aqueos systems and the thermodynamic factors operating in it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hydrogen ion numbers are maintained to a minimum by the following thermodynamic factors: (1) the water of reaction is kept at a minimum, (2) the partition coefficient of lactic acid between water and organic solvent is kept high, (3) the dissociation of lactic acid in the water of the microaquoeus phase is kept at a maximum and (4) the esterification is kept at a high value.
, the hydrogen ions are generated in the microaqueoues phase from the dissociation of water-soluble lactic acid in the presence of the enzyme.

the hydrogen ion concentration in the microaqueoues phase is maintained by the following thermodynamic processes: (1) the partitioning of the acid between the organic solvent and the microaqueoue phase, (2) the dissolution of the acid in the microaqueouse phase and (3) the dissociation of the dissolved acid in the microaquaeous phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microaqueous water phase in non-aqueus media is an important factor in lipase catalysing the esterification reaction and that it is the microaqueous hydrogen ion concentration which determines the maximum substrate concentration at a given amount of lipase in a given organic solvent.
the hydrogen ions in microaqueoues phase are the major cause for the decrease in the catalytic activity of the lipase.
the hydrogen ion number is a function of the substrate concentration and the number of hydrogen ions in the microaqueos phase is maintained to a minimum by the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microaqueous water phase is a dynamic system where the number of hydrogen ions in the microaqueouse phase is maintained to a minimum by the various thermodynamic processes which operate at the microaqueouse-water-solvent interface.

the number of hydrogen ions at the microaqueoues phase can be controlled by the thermodynamic process of acid partitioning between water and solvent, and the number of H+ in the microaqueouos phase can be reduced by lowering the substrate concentrations.
the hydrogen ion concentration in the microaqueou phase can be maintained below the critical value for the lipase by proper selection of the substrate concentration and the water of the reaction.
